requirement.summary: Action 5 / POS282: BIR Sales Summary Report
requirement.description:
Reference: Epic attachment bir_data_process_and_report_revamp_proposal.pdf — Action 5 (bir_sales_summary).

Scope:

- Refactor bir_sales_summary (MySQL + SQL Server) to read new standard tables.

- Use 3-table UNION (pos_bir_station_summaries + pos_bir_station_monthly_summaries + pos_bir_station_summaries_temporary) + JOIN pos_bir_daily_infos for cumulative fields.

- Support year-to-date / since-opening via Action 4 on-demand routing.

- Station/payment display names resolved at report runtime from POS master data.
requirement.release_notes:
Enhancement: [HERO-68284,HERO-68285,HERO-68286,HERO-68287,HERO-68288,HERO-68289,HERO-69412] Update BIR reports to read new standard tables (summary and detail)
Description:
-      [POS282] BIR Sales Summary Report (MySQL & MSSQL)
-      [POS063] Revenue Report (Philippines) (MySQL & MSSQL)
-      [POS060] BIR Report (Philippines) (MySQL & MSSQL)
-      [CUS012] BIR Report (Philippines) (By Running Number) (MySQL only)
-      [CUS313] BIR-EIS Sales Summary Report (MySQL & MSSQL)
-      [CUS314] BIR-EIS BIR Detail Report (Philippines) (MySQL & MSSQL)
-      [POS081] BIR Detail Report (Philippines) (MySQL & MSSQL)
-      Refactor the above BIR reports (Epic HERO-68279) so formal rptdesign files read the new standard pos_bir_* tables instead of legacy rpt_dyn_pos_bir_* dynamic tables.
-      Summary reports use the shared three-table UNION (pos_bir_station_summaries + pos_bir_station_monthly_summaries + pos_bir_station_summaries_temporary), joining pos_bir_daily_infos for running numbers / cumulative fields where needed; display names (station, payment) resolve from POS master data at runtime.
-      Detail reports read pos_bir_check_payments (within retention) or pos_bir_check_payments_temporary (on-demand), one row per payment / running number; they do not use monthly summaries and do not support since-opening (max range 3 months, enforced by Report Module on-demand routing).
-      Each report delivers a transitional _legacy.rptdesign (still reads rpt_dyn_*) alongside the formal design. Until migration completes, the Report Module routes to the legacy file; after migration completes, it uses the formal file. On-demand UI is enabled only when the transitional legacy design is present and the report is listed for on-demand.
-      Date-range routing and on-demand queueing are handled by the Report Module and report engine; preprocess / temporary table generation are handled by BirPreprocessShell.
Configuration / Parameter:
-      No new report parameters are added. Existing date range and filter parameters are unchanged.
-      Open a covered BIR report from POS Module > Desktop Format. When the selected range is within retention, the viewer renders directly; when any date is older than retention, the viewer routes to the On-Demand job form.
-      Admin Console > System Configuration > Report Module: “Auto-cleanup On-Demand jobs” (Yes/No) soft-deletes the temporary preset and related one-time scheduled tasks after the on-demand report is sent.
Field Definition:
-      This case does not involve field definition. Layout columns keep the existing dpbb_* / dpbp_* aliases; only the SQL data source changes.
Result / Sample:
-      Open a summary report (example: POS060 BIR Report (Philippines) / bir_ph) and set Date type to “Specified as below” with a range older than the last 3 months (example: 2026-01-01 ~ 2026-03-31).
-      The report engine shows “Background generation required” and lists monthly segments for on-demand generation.
-      Click “Add to generation queue” to open the On-Demand Job form (email interface, recipients, format). After submit, the result page shows the created Preset Parameters id and Scheduled Task ids.
-      Preset Parameters listing shows the on-demand preset (e.g. “On-demand POS060 2026-01-01 2026-03-31”); Report Management > Scheduled Tasks lists the one-time BirPreprocessShell tasks for each month segment.
-      After preprocess and AutoReport complete, the emailed report is produced from the formal design reading pos_bir_* ∪ temporary tables. Within retention, the same formal design renders directly without on-demand.
-      For a detail report (example: POS081 BIR Detail Report (Philippines) / bir_detail_ph), repeat with a range beyond retention but within 3 months: on-demand writes pos_bir_check_payments_temporary for the full range (no monthly segment reuse); ranges over 3 months are rejected.
-      Before migration completes, opening the same report uses the transitional *_legacy design against rpt_dyn_*; after migration status is completed, the formal design is used automatically.
